newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican media mogul Azcarraga dies of cancer.
newsitem.headline: Mexican media mogul Azcarraga dies of cancer.

text.p: Emilio Azcarraga Milmo, former head of Mexico's Grupo Televisa and Latin America's top media mogul, died on Wednesday of cancer, Televisa said.

The 66-year-old billionaire, who during two decades at its helm built Televisa into the Spanish speaking world's largest media firm, died in Miami, Florida, Televisa said in its 24 Horas nightly bulletin.
His body was due to be flown back to Mexico for burial.
"He had his life and now begins the legend," 24 Horas anchorman Jacobo Zabludovsky said when announcing the death of the man he called "Our Boss," his face marked by grief.

Azcarraga, who stepped down as chairman of Televisa in March due to ill health, had a hard-nosed business acumen that made him one of the richest men in Latin America worth some $2 billion last year, according to Forbes Magazine.

He was also an unabashed promoter of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) which has ruled Mexico for 68 years. Critics said his news programs were often slanted to help the PRI in elections and to trash the opposition.

During a fund-raising banquet by former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari in 1993, Azcarraga was widely reported in the Mexican press to have offered $50 million to help the PRI's re-election efforts.

President Ernesto Zedillo mourned his death, describing Azcarraga in a statement as "a great businessman with a trajectory in the world of communication, artistic entertainment and sport who gave Mexico international prestige."

His death was also lamented by opposition leaders. Carlos Castillo Peraza, ex-head of the conservative National Action Party, told a Televisa radio station on Wednesday that Azcarraga had begun to contribute to Mexico's democratic opening towards the end of his life.
In the Mexican stock market, where Televisa is one of the biggest issuers, news of his death was expected to come as a shock on Thursday.

Though he stepped down on March 3, and handed the reins over to his 29-year-old son Emilio Azcarraga Jean and Guillermo Canedo White, 37, many analysts had hoped he would continue to play a strong behind-the-scenes role.

Known as "The Tiger", Azcarraga took over from his father Emilio Azcarraga Vidaurrieta in 1972, and built Televisa up to include four television networks and dozens of radio stations, with revenues of some $1.4 billion last year.
It has also become one of the world's largest producers of soap operas, that Azcarraga defended as a crucial means of escape for poor Mexicans.
Besides his son, Azcarraga is survived by three daughters and his fifth wife, Adriana Abascal.
